takes.text: On her first day at school, Tani held her mother’s hand very tight. The classroom was big and noisy. Tani wanted to cry. Then a girl with red ribbons came and said: “Hello! I am Ewi. Do you want to play with the blocks?” Tani built a tall tower with Ewi. When her mother came back, Tani said: “Mummy, tomorrow I am coming back to play with Ewi!”

Do you want to play with the blocks?” Tani built a tall tower with Ewi. When her mother came back, Tani said: “Mummy, tomorrow I am coming back to play with Ewi!”

takes.text:
Two little hands go clap, clap, clap,
Two little feet go tap, tap, tap,
Two little eyes can see, see, see,
One little nose, and that is me!
segments: Two little hands go clap, clap, clap, Two little feet go tap, tap, tap, Two little eyes can see, see, see, One little nose, and that is me!

takes.text: Grandmother was cooking a big pot of rice for the whole family. “Who will help me?” she asked. “Not me, I am playing,” said Fon. “I will!” said little Bih, and she brought water and washed the plates. When the food was ready, everybody came to eat. Grandmother smiled at Bih: “Thank you for helping. A family is strong when everyone helps.” The next day, Fon came first to bring the water.

takes.text:
Ten little candles on a birthday cake,
Blow, blow, blow, one goes out, for goodness’ sake!
Nine little candles… (go on to one)
No more candles, let us eat the cake!
segments: Ten little candles on a birthday cake, Blow, blow, blow, one goes out, for goodness’ sake! Nine little candles… (go on to one) No more candles, let us eat the cake!

takes.text: A little seed slept under the soil. “Wake up!” said the rain, and gave it water. “Wake up!” said the sun, and gave it warmth. The seed stretched a tiny root down and a little green shoot up. Every day Ngwa watered it. One morning, there was a beautiful yellow flower, and Ngwa danced with joy.
segments: A little seed slept under the soil. “Wake up!” said the rain, and gave it water. “Wake up!” said the sun, and gave it warmth. The seed stretched a tiny root down and a little green shoot up. Every day Ngwa watered it. One morning, there was a beautiful yellow flower, and Ngwa danced with joy.

takes.text:
Little goat, little goat, with a bell on your coat,
You eat green grass and you jump on a rock,
Meh, meh, little goat, it is time to go home,
To sleep near the house when the night has come.
segments: Little goat, little goat, with a bell on your coat, You eat green grass and you jump on a rock, Meh, meh, little goat, it is time to go home, To sleep near the house when the night has come.

takes.text: Every night, while the town sleeps, Ewane the baker wakes up. He mixes flour, water and salt in a big bowl. He kneads the dough, push and fold, push and fold. He puts the bread in the hot oven. In the morning, the whole street smells good, and the children say: “Thank you, Ewane, for our bread!”
segments: Every night, while the town sleeps, Ewane the baker wakes up. He mixes flour, water and salt in a big bowl. He kneads the dough, push and fold, push and fold. He puts the bread in the hot oven. In the morning, the whole street smells good, and the children say: “Thank you, Ewane, for our bread!”

takes.text:
Beep, beep, says the little bus,
The wheels go round, there is room for us,
Stop at the market, stop at the school,
Sit down quietly, that is the rule!
segments: Beep, beep, says the little bus, The wheels go round, there is room for us, Stop at the market, stop at the school, Sit down quietly, that is the rule!

takes.text: At break time, Eno looked for his lunch box. It was not in his bag! He looked under the bench, near the door, behind the cupboard. His friend Mbong saw that he was sad… (stop and ask) …Mbong said: “Come, we can share my sandwich.” After break, the teacher found the lunch box on the windowsill. The next day, Eno brought two bananas: one for him and one for Mbong.

takes.text:
Ten little fingers to hold my spoon,
Ten little toes to dance to the tune,
Ten and ten, let us count them, friends:
Twenty little helpers at my ends!
segments: Ten little fingers to hold my spoon, Ten little toes to dance to the tune, Ten and ten, let us count them, friends: Twenty little helpers at my ends!

takes.text:
Two red balloons, four, six, eight,
Ten at the door, we cannot wait!
Twelve, fourteen, sixteen in the air,
Eighteen, twenty, balloons everywhere!
segments: Two red balloons, four, six, eight, Ten at the door, we cannot wait! Twelve, fourteen, sixteen in the air, Eighteen, twenty, balloons everywhere!

takes.text: Early in the morning, the cock said: “Cock-a-doodle-doo!” The goat woke up: “Meh, meh!” The cow mooed: “Moo!” The dog barked: “Woof, woof!” But the little pig was still sleeping. All the animals called together, very loudly. The little pig opened one eye and said: “Oink! Is it already morning?” And everybody laughed.

All the animals called together, very loudly. The little pig opened one eye and said: “Oink! Is it already morning?” And everybody laughed.

takes.text:
Mango, mango, on the tree,
Green today, but wait and see,
Yellow, sweet and soft one day,
We will share it, hip hooray!
segments: Mango, mango, on the tree, Green today, but wait and see, Yellow, sweet and soft one day, We will share it, hip hooray!

takes.text: Madam Ebude, the tailor, had to sew ten school uniforms for Monday. On Saturday her sewing machine broke! She sat down and was very worried… (stop and ask) …Her neighbour, the mechanic, came with his tools and repaired the machine. Madam Ebude worked all Sunday, and on Monday the children were proud of their new uniforms.

takes.text:
Vroom goes the car on the long, long road,
Toot goes the truck with a heavy load,
Choo-choo goes the train, swish goes the boat,
And up in the sky the planes all float!
